subject: Recap and procurement path — inference sizing & monthly spend validation for Atlas Retail
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@atlasretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap and procurement path — inference sizing & monthly spend validation for Atlas Retail

Hi Marco / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great conversation. This is a quick post-call recap so we have aligned expectations on monthly token volumes, target unit economics, and the procurement thresholds you mentioned. 

Quick summary of what we covered on the call:
- Workload: 2 primary features (search re-ranker + chat assist). Estimated steady-state generation: ~150-250M tokens/month depending on traffic growth and prompts.
- Quality target: aiming for parity with current on-prem ranking model; we recommended a 13B dense model variant for re-rank and a 7B chat model for assist in initial rollout.
- Pricing objective: target unit economics in the ballpark of $350–$700 per 1M tokens (range reflects model variant and quantization).
- Procurement constraints you flagged: single PO max ~$25k; preference for NET30; need SOC 2 excerpt and short SOW for procurement.

Action items I committed to:
1) Share a constrained-cost scenario and a growth scenario with explicit monthly spend bands and per-1M-token math.
2) Attach SOC2 excerpt and the current pricing worksheet for internal procurement review.
3) Propose a procurement path if a single PO cap blocks the monthly spend required.

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet) and SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf (excerpt).

Next immediate ask for you: can you confirm whether the $25k single-PO cap is absolute, or if you can accept split POs/incremental monthly invoices from a single vendor? Also confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).

I'll include a short table below with two modeled bands (conservative / growth) so procurement can see concrete numbers.

Modeled spend bands (illustrative):
- Conservative: 100M tokens/month • Estimated spend: $35k–$70k/month (using $350–$700 per 1M tokens)
- Growth: 250M tokens/month • Estimated spend: $87.5k–$175k/month

If the single-PO cap is indeed $25k and cannot be changed, we can discuss purchasing a multi-month prepay or using a reseller route (we have marketplace and channel partners who can invoice differently).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an explicit purchase-path proposal once I hear your PO constraints.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com]
[attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[attachment: SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@atlasretail.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap and procurement path — inference sizing & monthly spend validation for Atlas Retail

Thanks Jasmine — useful recap. A couple clarifications from procurement side:

- The $25k single-PO cap is our preferred internal threshold for direct vendor contracts. It is not impossible to raise, but requires director-level approval and typically takes 3–4 weeks.
- We can accept NET30.
- Splitting into multiple POs for the same product is allowed but we need the invoices tied to separate deliverable dates.
- Prepayment is allowed but will need a business justification memo.

From an ops perspective, the team is comfortable with the projected token ranges you sent. For planning, assume we will start around 120M tokens/month in month 1 and ramp to 200–220M/month over three months.

Can you send: a) an example SOW (1 page) we can use in the procurement packet, and b) a proposal that shows a 3-month prepay at a discount vs. a monthly bill scenario (just the numbers)?

Thanks,
Marco Alvarez
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Retail

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@atlasretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap and procurement path — inference sizing & monthly spend validation for Atlas Retail

Appreciate the quick reply Marco — hope that timing works. Attached is a 1-page SOW template and an updated pricing worksheet with two explicit procurement-friendly proposals:

Option A — Monthly billing (flexible):
- Unit price: $425 per 1M tokens (mid-range estimate for the recommended mix of models with quantized runtime)
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing, NET30
- For 120M tokens: ~ $51,000/month
- For 200M tokens: ~ $85,000/month

Option B — 3-month prepay (discounted):
- Effective unit price: $375 per 1M tokens (5–12% discount depending on exact committed volume)
- Upfront invoice(s) can be split across multiple POs if you need separate deliverable dates — we can map the prepay to three monthly consumption reports for your finance team.
- 120M tokens/month x 3 months (360M total) at $375/1M => $135,000 upfront (can be split into 3 x $45k POs)

Procurement workaround notes:
- If the $25k PO cap is firm, splitting into multiple POs is the fastest path; each PO needs a separate deliverable or billing date, which you indicated is acceptable.
- Alternatively, we can engage a channel partner (marketplace reseller) who can accept smaller PO sizes and invoice on a consumption basis; this can also simplify internal approvals.

Attached files in this message: 1-page_SOW_for_Atlas.docx (SOW template), redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (detailed bands), SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
1) Let procurement confirm whether they want a 3x $45k PO plan (splits the prepay into procurement-friendly buckets) or a single monthly billing path.
2) If prepay route, we can provide a short business justification memo for your director to accelerate above-$25k approvals (Aditya, happy to draft and co-sign).
3) I'll prepare a draft DocuSign quote once procurement confirms route and billing addresses.

If useful I can also join a quick procurement call to walk the AP team through invoice timing.

Best,
Jasmine
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com]
[attachment: 1-page_SOW_for_Atlas.docx (docx)]
[attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[attachment: SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Recap and procurement path — inference sizing & monthly spend validation for Atlas Retail

Thanks for the tidy proposal Jasmine. A couple internal notes for our approach:

- Approve offering a 3-month prepay with the split-PO structure to unblock procurement quickly. We can field any director-level questions with the business justification memo (I will review and sign).
- Recommend offering a 1-month onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first invoice to lower the first-month sticker shock (we have room for this in our enterprise playbook for deals this size).
- Rachel: please update the HubSpot deal to "Contracting — Prepay agreed" once Marco confirms the split-PO plan. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345

Jasmine: once Marco confirms the PO-splitting approach, send the DocuSign quote and include the onboarding credit line item.

Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
